To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is considerable long run income inequality in Sweden, (2) this inequality is not due to circumstances alone, (3) it is due to circumstances to some degree, and (4) it is mainly due to individual effort.

(i) in Sweden, given current social policy and institutions, the distribution of long term income is highly unequal, (ii) a large part of that inequality is due to differences in effort, and (iii) a smaller part of the inequality is due to circumstances.

the Swedish society, in spite of its high degree of social equality, has achieved a high degree of equality of opportunity, and that this equality of opportunity is due to the high degree of individual effort.

a question that has received much attention in recent years: to what extent is inequality of income due to circumstances, and to what extent is it due to individual effort?
the question: to what extent is the distribution of income in Sweden today due to circumstances, and to what extent is it due to individual choices and personal effort?
